questions.question: Who is the Chairperson of the 16th Finance Commission of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Arvind Panagariya**__**.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **N. K. Singh** was the Chairperson of the **15th Finance Commission** and is a notable economist and policymaker in India.
 
• The **16th Finance Commission** has been constituted as of the latest updates. The Chairperson of the 16th Finance Commission of India is Dr. Arvind Panagariya. 
 
• The Chairperson of a Finance Commission is typically an expert in public finance, economics, or administration, ensuring that the recommendations align with national priorities.
 
• **N. K. Singh**, as the Chairperson of the 15th Finance Commission, played a significant role in addressing critical financial issues such as **tax devolution, grants to local bodies, and disaster management funds.**
 
• The Finance Commission is a constitutional body established under **Article 280 of the Indian Constitution**, which ensures a sound fiscal relationship between the **Union and the States.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **About the Finance Commission:**

 
 
• The Finance Commission is a **constitutional body** constituted by the President of India every **five years** under **Article 280**.
 
• Its primary function is to recommend the division of **tax revenues** between the **Union and the States** and among the states themselves.
 
• It also addresses issues related to **grants-in-aid** for local bodies and other financial matters as referred to it by the President.
 
 
 
• **Key Responsibilities of the Chairperson:**
 
 
• To lead discussions on **fiscal policies** and ensure equitable revenue sharing between the Union and States.
 
• To analyze and address economic challenges, such as **fiscal deficits, state debts, and revenue mobilization.**
 
• To guide the Commission in providing recommendations for financial governance and intergovernmental fiscal relations.
 
 
 
• **About N. K. Singh:**
 
 
• Nand Kishore Singh is a prominent Indian economist, policymaker, and former IAS officer.
 
• He has held key positions, including **Revenue Secretary** and **Expenditure Secretary** in the Government of India.
 
• As Chairperson of the 15th Finance Commission, he addressed vital issues such as **vertical and horizontal tax devolution, local body finances, and disaster management funds.**
 
 
 
• **Article 280 of the Constitution:**
 
 
• This Article mandates the formation of the Finance Commission by the President every five years or earlier, as required.
 
• The Commission consists of a **Chairperson** and four other members appointed by the President.
 
• Its recommendations are advisory, but they carry significant weight in shaping fiscal policies and governance.
 
 
 
• **Historical Background:**
 
 
• The first Finance Commission was constituted in **1951** under the Chairmanship of **K.C. Neogy**.
 
• Since then, 15 Finance Commissions have been constituted, addressing India's evolving fiscal needs and governance challenges.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **15th Finance Commission Recommendations:**

 
 
• Vertical devolution of **41% of the divisible tax pool** to states, a reduction from 42% due to Jammu & Kashmir's reorganization.
 
• Special grants and performance-based incentives for states to improve governance and fiscal management.
 
• Focus on **health, education, and disaster risk management** in fiscal transfers.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Finance Commissions:**
 
 
• They ensure a balanced fiscal relationship between **different levels of government.**
 
• They promote financial stability and equitable development across regions in India.
 
• They help address fiscal challenges like **debt sustainability and resource mobilization** in a growing economy.

questions.question: Which keyboard shortcut permanently deletes a file without sending it to the Recycle Bin in Windows OS?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shift + Delete**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Shift + Delete** keyboard shortcut in Windows OS permanently deletes a file without sending it to the Recycle Bin.
 
• This action bypasses the Recycle Bin, making recovery of the file more difficult unless specialized software is used.
 
• It is a quick method to remove unwanted files permanently and save disk space.
 
• Users are advised to exercise caution while using this shortcut, as accidental deletions may require advanced recovery tools.
 
• Files deleted using this method do not consume space in the Recycle Bin and are immediately removed from the file system.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Recycle Bin**

 
 
• The Recycle Bin is a feature in Windows OS used to temporarily store deleted files.
 
• Files moved to the Recycle Bin can be restored unless the bin is emptied.
 
• It serves as a safeguard against accidental deletions.
 
 
 
• **File Recovery**
 
 
• Files permanently deleted using **Shift + Delete** can sometimes be recovered using third-party recovery tools.
 
• Examples of such tools include Recuva, EaseUS Data Recovery Wizard, and Disk Drill.
 
 
 
• **File System**
 
 
• The file system in Windows OS (e.g., NTFS, FAT32) manages how data is stored and retrieved on storage devices.
 
• Permanently deleted files are marked as free space in the file system and may be overwritten by new data.
 
 
 
• **Best Practices**
 
 
• Always double-check before using **Shift + Delete** to ensure important files are not deleted accidentally.
 
• Maintain regular backups to avoid permanent data loss.

questions.question: In modern CPUs, what technique is used to execute multiple instructions simultaneously?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pipelining**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Pipelining** is a technique used in modern CPUs to execute multiple instructions simultaneously by dividing them into stages.
 
• Each stage of the pipeline performs a specific operation (e.g., fetch, decode, execute, etc.) to process instructions concurrently.
 
• Pipelining improves the **instruction throughput**, allowing the CPU to complete more instructions per unit time.
 
• The technique is widely used in **RISC (Reduced Instruction Set Computer)** architectures for enhanced performance.
 
• Pipeline efficiency depends on factors like **branch prediction**, **data hazards**, and **instruction dependencies**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Clock Synchronization**:

 
 
• Ensures all parts of a CPU operate in sync with the system clock.
 
• It does not execute multiple instructions simultaneously but coordinates timing between processes.
 
 
 
• **Sequential Execution**:
 
 
• A traditional processing method where instructions are executed one after the other.
 
• This method contrasts with parallel execution techniques like pipelining.
 
 
 
• **Hazards in Pipelining**:
 
 
• **Data Hazards:** Occur when instructions depend on the results of previous ones.
 
• **Control Hazards:** Arise due to branch instructions affecting the flow of execution.
 
• **Structural Hazards:** Result from resource conflicts within the pipeline.
 
 
 
• **Parallel Processing vs Pipelining**:
 
 
• Parallel processing uses multiple processors to execute tasks simultaneously.
 
• Pipelining divides a single processor's tasks into stages for concurrent execution.

questions.question:
An element ‘A’ reacts with water to form a solution. This solution turns phenolphthalein indicator pink.

Which of the following could be element ‘A’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sodium**__.

__**Concept**__:

__
 
• **Indicators **are solutions of substances that show different colours in acidic, basic, and neutral solutions.
 
• In acid-base titrations, phenolphthalein is commonly used as an indicator.

**Explanation:**__

 
• Phenolphthalein has acidic groups (hydroxyl groups). These groups are acidic in nature, they do not react with the acid added to the solution, and no ions are formed. This is why, when an acid is added to phenolphthalein, the colour does not change.
 
• In the presence of a base, the phenolphthalein solution turns pink. This is due to the fact that the hydroxide ions react with the acidic group present, resulting in the formation of ions. These ions colourize the solution.
 
• Sodium is a metal that can react with water to form Sodium hydroxide, a basic compound in nature. Hence, the phenolphthalein solution turns pink.

questions.question: Yakshagana is a folk theatre form from which of the following States of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Karnataka**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Yakshagana** is a traditional folk theatre form that originated in Karnataka, India.
 
• This theatre form combines **dance, music, dialogue, costume, and makeup** into a unique cultural expression.
 
• Yakshagana performances are often based on stories from **Hindu epics** such as the Ramayana, Mahabharata, and the Puranas.
 
• The art form is primarily performed in districts like **Udupi, Dakshina Kannada, Uttara Kannada, Shimoga, and Kasaragod** (in Kerala).
 
• Yakshagana is typically performed overnight, starting in the evening and continuing until dawn, with artists engaging in elaborate storytelling and dramatic enactment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Yakshagana Terminology:**

 
 
• **Himmela:** Refers to the background musicians, including percussionists and vocalists.
 
• **Mummela:** Refers to the actors and dancers performing on stage.
 
• **Chande:** A traditional drum used in Yakshagana performances.
 
• **Bhagavata:** The lead singer and storyteller who narrates the story and sets the tone for the performance.
 
 
 
• **Costumes and Makeup:** Yakshagana is known for its elaborate costumes, colorful headgear, and intricate facial makeup that represent various mythological characters.
 
• **Historical Background:** Yakshagana is believed to have originated as early as the 10th century, evolving from temple rituals and traditional storytelling practices.
 
• **Contemporary Relevance:** Yakshagana remains an important cultural symbol of Karnataka, with performances often organized during festivals and cultural events.
 
• **Training and Preservation:** Institutions and academies in Karnataka continue to teach and preserve Yakshagana, ensuring the survival of this ancient art form.

questions.question: The second home for Cheetahs in India (after Kuno) has been identified in which wildlife sanctuary of Madhya Pradesh?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gandhi Sagar Wildlife Sanctuary**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Gandhi Sagar Wildlife Sanctuary, located in Madhya Pradesh, has been identified as the second site for the reintroduction of cheetahs in India after Kuno National Park.
 
• This sanctuary is spread across parts of Mandsaur and Neemuch districts and is known for its diverse flora and fauna, offering a suitable habitat for cheetahs.
 
• The decision to identify Gandhi Sagar Wildlife Sanctuary as a cheetah habitat is part of India’s ambitious Project Cheetah, aimed at reintroducing the species after its extinction in the country.
 
• The sanctuary has abundant grasslands and open spaces, which are ideal for cheetahs to thrive and hunt, making it a preferred location for this project.
 
• Extensive preparation and habitat assessment have been carried out to ensure the sanctuary can support cheetah populations sustainably, including minimizing human-wildlife conflict.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Satpura National Park:**

 
 
• Located in the Hoshangabad district of Madhya Pradesh, Satpura National Park is known for its unique terrain, including sandstone peaks, dense forests, and deep ravines.
 
• It is part of the Satpura Tiger Reserve and houses a significant population of tigers, leopards, and other wildlife.
 
• However, Satpura National Park has not been identified for the cheetah reintroduction project due to its dense forest cover, which is less suitable for cheetahs, who prefer open grasslands for hunting.
 
 
 
• **Panna National Park:**
 
 
• Panna National Park is located in the Panna and Chhatarpur districts of Madhya Pradesh and is famous for its tiger conservation efforts under the Project Tiger initiative.
 
• The park is known for its riverine forests and diverse wildlife, including tigers, leopards, and gharials.
 
• While it is a prominent wildlife sanctuary, it does not meet the specific habitat requirements for cheetahs, such as open grasslands and minimal forest cover.
 
 
 
• **Sanjay-Dubri National Park:**
 
 
• Sanjay-Dubri National Park is situated in the Sidhi district of Madhya Pradesh and forms part of the Sanjay Tiger Reserve.
 
• It is home to various wildlife species, including tigers, leopards, and chital.
 
• The park's dense forests and rugged terrain are not ideal for cheetah reintroduction, which requires large open spaces for their survival and hunting.
 
 
 
• **Project Cheetah:**
 
 
• Project Cheetah is an initiative of the Indian government to reintroduce cheetahs, which became extinct in India in 1952, back into the wild.
 
• Under this project, eight cheetahs were brought to Kuno National Park in Madhya Pradesh from Namibia in 2022.
 
• The project aims to establish a metapopulation of cheetahs across multiple sites in India to ensure their long-term survival.
 
• The identification of Gandhi Sagar Wildlife Sanctuary as the second site is a significant step in expanding the scope of this initiative.
